literal: Xianzu, Emperor Xianwen, bore the taboo name Hong; he was Gaozong, Emperor Wencheng's eldest son; his mother was Lady Li, Honored Person.
idiomatic: Xianzu, Emperor Xianwen, bore the taboo name Hong. He was the eldest son of Gaozong, Emperor Wencheng; his mother was Lady Li, Honored Person.

literal: First year of Xingguang, autumn, seventh month: he was born north of Yinshan.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn of the first year of Xingguang he was born north of Yinshan.

literal: Second year of Tai'an, second month: he was installed as crown prince.
idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Tai'an he was installed as crown prince.

literal: Clever, perceptive, and quick of wit, in youth he already had a design to succor the people with divine martial prowess; pure in benevolence and filial piety, he honored teachers and friends with ritual courtesy.
idiomatic: Clever, perceptive, and quick of wit, even as a boy he showed a mind to succor the people with divine martial prowess. Pure in benevolence and filial piety, he honored teachers and friends with ritual courtesy.

literal: Sixth year of Heping, summer, fifth month, day jiachen: he assumed the imperial throne; a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer of the sixth year of Heping, on the jiachen day, he took the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.

literal: The empress was honored as empress dowager.
idiomatic: The empress was honored as empress dowager.

literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Yi Hun forged an edict and killed Minister of the Masters of Writing Yang Baonian, Duke of Pingyang Jia Airen, and Duke of Nanyang Zhang Tiandu within the inner palace.
idiomatic: Yi Hun, General of Chariots and Cavalry, forged an edict and killed Yang Baonian, Minister of the Masters of Writing, Jia Airen, Duke of Pingyang, and Zhang Tiandu, Duke of Nanyang, within the inner palace.

literal: Day wushen: Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of Works, Prince of Pingyuan Lu Li entered court from Tangquan; Hun killed him as well.
idiomatic: On the wushen day Lu Li, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of Works, and Prince of Pingyuan, came to court from Tangquan; Yi Hun killed him as well.

literal: Day jiyou: Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Chariots and Cavalry Yi Hun was made Grand Commandant and Recorder of Secretariat Affairs; Prince of Dong'an Liu Ni was made Minister of the Masses; Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing He Qinu was made Minister of Works.
idiomatic: On the jiyou day Yi Hun, Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Chariots and Cavalry, was made Grand Commandant and Recorder of Secretariat Affairs; Liu Ni, Prince of Dong'an, was made Minister of the Masses; and He Qinu, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Minister of Works.

literal: Day renzi: Prince of Huainan Ta was made Grand General Who Guards the West, with Equipage Equal to the Three Directors, and garrisoned Liangzhou.
idiomatic: On the renzi day Prince of Huainan Ta was made Grand General Who Guards the West with equipage equal to the Three Directors and posted to garrison Liangzhou.

literal: Sixth month: Marquis of Fanyang Li Ni was enfeoffed as Prince of Danyang; General Who Conquers the East Feng Xi was enfeoffed as Prince of Changli.
idiomatic: In the sixth month Li Ni, Marquis of Fanyang, was enfeoffed as Prince of Danyang, and Feng Xi, General Who Conquers the East, as Prince of Changli.

literal: Day yichou: an edict stated: "When levies and collections are burdensome the people's wealth is exhausted; when assessments and imposts are light expenditures are insufficient—hence the one-tenth tax, and songs of praise arose.
idiomatic: On the yichou day an edict stated, "When levies and collections are burdensome the people's wealth is exhausted; when assessments are too light the treasury falls short—hence the one-tenth tax, and songs of praise arose.

literal: The former court weighed their lightness and heaviness to benefit the hundred surnames.
idiomatic: The former court weighed their burden to benefit the common people.

literal: We inherit the great enterprise, looking up to the ancestors' mandate of blessing; rising early and awaiting dawn, we think only of the people's hardship, wishing to make all under Heaven share in ease and delight.
idiomatic: We inherit the great enterprise and look up to the ancestors' mandate of blessing. Rising early and awaiting dawn, we think only of the people's hardship, wishing to make all under Heaven share in ease and delight.

literal: Yet corvée and levies do not cease—how shall we block excess, remove harshness, and rescue the black-haired masses!
idiomatic: Yet corvée and levies do not cease—how shall we block excess, remove harshness, and rescue the common people!

literal: Now arms are not raised and stores are abundant; all miscellaneous levies are hereby remitted to the people."
idiomatic: Now arms are not raised and stores are abundant; all miscellaneous levies are hereby remitted to the people."

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day guisi: Grand Commandant Yi Hun was made Chancellor, ranking above all princes; great and small affairs were all decided by Hun.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the guisi day, Grand Commandant Yi Hun was made chancellor, ranking above all princes; great and small affairs were all decided by Yi Hun.

literal: Ninth month, day gengzi: a partial amnesty was proclaimed in the capital.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the gengzi day, a partial amnesty was proclaimed in the capital.

literal: Day bingwu: an edict stated: "The former court, because provincial governors are close to the people, should appoint worthy assistants; therefore it charged the offices with promulgating the Nine Articles, making the outgoing administration select officials to await the worthy and able, [1] surely meaning that the scales of office would be even-handed and court discipline properly ordered.
idiomatic: On the bingwu day an edict stated, "The former court held that because provincial governors are close to the people they should appoint worthy assistants; therefore it charged the offices with promulgating the Nine Articles, making the outgoing administration select officials to await the worthy and able, [1] surely meaning that the scales of office would be even-handed and court discipline properly ordered.

literal: Yet the governors and inspectors were lax and remiss, not revering the charter's intent; they recommended unworthy men and transgressed the statutes.
idiomatic: Yet the governors and inspectors were lax and remiss and did not reverence the charter's intent; they recommended unworthy men and transgressed the statutes.

literal: The present regulation: when governors and magistrates arrive at their posts, they are to nominate men of local repute who are loyal and trustworthy to serve as selection officials; they may not collude with the outgoing administration.
idiomatic: The present regulation is this: when governors and magistrates arrive at their posts, they are to nominate men of local repute who are loyal and trustworthy to serve as selection officials, and may not collude with the outgoing administration.

literal: If selection and appointment miss the mark, they are to be judged for deceiving the throne."
idiomatic: If selection and appointment miss the mark, they are to be judged for deceiving the throne."

literal: " That month Liu Ziye's General Who Campaigns North, Prince of Yiyang Liu Chang, came from Pengcheng to surrender.
idiomatic: That month Liu Chang, Liu Ziye's General Who Campaigns North and Prince of Yiyang, came from Pengcheng to surrender.

literal: Winter, tenth month: Prince of Yangping Xincheng, Prince of Jingzhao Zitui, Prince of Jiyin Xiaoxincheng, Prince of Ruyin Tiansi, and Prince of Rencheng Yun were summoned to court.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Princes Xincheng of Yangping, Zitui of Jingzhao, Xiaoxincheng of Jiyin, Tiansi of Ruyin, and Yun of Rencheng were summoned to court.

literal: First year of Tian'an, spring, first month, day yichou first of month: a general amnesty; the era name was changed.
idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the first year of Tian'an, on the yichou day, the new moon, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.

literal: Second month, day gengshen: Chancellor, Prince of Taiyuan Yi Hun plotted rebellion and was executed.
idiomatic: In the second month, on the gengshen day, Yi Hun, chancellor and Prince of Taiyuan, plotted rebellion and was executed.

literal: Day yihai: Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Kongque was made Prince of Puyang; Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu Dingguo was made Prince of Dongjun.
idiomatic: On the yihai day Yuan Kongque, Attendant-in-Ordinary, was made Prince of Puyang, and Lu Dingguo, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Prince of Dongjun.

literal: Third month, day gengzi: Yuan He of Longxi was made Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: In the third month, on the gengzi day, Yuan He of Longxi was made Grand Commandant.

literal: Day xinchou: the spirit tablet of Gaozong, Emperor Wencheng, was associated in the Grand Temple.
idiomatic: On the xinchou day the spirit tablet of Gaozong, Emperor Wencheng, was associated in the Grand Temple.

literal: Day xinhai: the Emperor visited the Dao altar and personally received talismans and registers;
idiomatic: On the xinhai day the emperor visited the Dao altar and personally received talismans and registers;

literal: a partial amnesty was proclaimed in the capital.
idiomatic: a partial amnesty was proclaimed in the capital.

literal: Goryeo, Persia, Khotan, Axi, and other states each sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: Goryeo, Persia, Khotan, Axi, and other states each sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day xinhai: an edict that all who had fraudulently obtained rank and title were specially pardoned but stripped of rank and office.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the xinhai day, an edict pardoned all who had fraudulently obtained rank and title but stripped them of rank and office.

literal: Those whose ancestors or fathers had borrowed titles and bribed to regularize their names were not permitted to succeed.
idiomatic: Those whose ancestors or fathers had borrowed titles and bribed to regularize their names were not permitted to succeed.

literal: All who had been promoted or transferred beyond merit were also each returned to their original status.
idiomatic: All who had been promoted or transferred beyond merit were likewise returned to their original status.

literal: Those who did not report truthfully were to be judged for great irreverence.
idiomatic: Those who did not report truthfully were to be judged for great irreverence.

literal: Ninth month: Liu Yu's Inspector of Sizhou Chang Zhenqi submitted Xuanhu inward.
idiomatic: In the ninth month Chang Zhenqi, Liu Yu's inspector of Sizhou, submitted Xuanhu to allegiance.

literal: Day jiyou: village schools were first established; each commandery was to have two Erudites, two teaching assistants, and sixty students.
idiomatic: On the jiyou day village schools were first established; each commandery was to have two Erudites, two teaching assistants, and sixty students.

literal: Liu Yu's Inspector of Xuzhou Xue Andu submitted Pengcheng inward; Liu Yu's generals Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi attacked Andu.
idiomatic: Xue Andu, Liu Yu's inspector of Xuzhou, submitted Pengcheng to allegiance; Liu Yu's generals Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi attacked him.

literal: An edict that Minister of the Northern Bureau Wei Yuan was Grand General Who Guards the South and Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs; General Who Guards the East, Duke of Chengyang Kong Bogong, was deputy; they marched by the eastern route to relieve Pengcheng;
idiomatic: An edict named Wei Yuan, Minister of the Northern Bureau, Grand General Who Guards the South and commander-in-chief of all military affairs, with Kong Bogong, General Who Guards the East and Duke of Chengyang, as deputy, to march by the eastern route to relieve Pengcheng;

literal: Palace Attendant of the Masters of Writing, Grand General Who Guards the West, Duke of Xihe Yuan Shi commanded the military affairs of Jing, Yu, and Southern Yong provinces; Palace Attendant Giving, Marquis of Jingzhao Zhang Qiongqi, was deputy; they marched by the western route to relieve Xuanhu.
idiomatic: Yuan Shi, Palace Attendant of the Masters of Writing, Grand General Who Guards the West, and Duke of Xihe, was to command the military affairs of Jing, Yu, and Southern Yong provinces, with Zhang Qiongqi, palace attendant giving and Marquis of Jingzhao, as deputy, to march by the western route to relieve Xuanhu.

literal: That year eleven provinces and garrisons suffered drought; the people were famished; granaries were opened for relief.
idiomatic: That year eleven provinces and garrisons suffered drought; the people were famished, and granaries were opened for relief.

literal: First year of Huangxing, spring, first month, day guisi: Wei Yuan greatly defeated Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi east of Lüliang; heads taken numbered in the tens of thousands; those who died of cold were very many.
idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the first year of Huangxing, on the guisi day, Wei Yuan greatly defeated Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi east of Lüliang; heads taken numbered in the tens of thousands, and very many died of cold.

literal: Liu Yu's Inspector of Qinzhou Yuan Gongzu and Feathered Forest Supervisor Shen Chengbo were captured.
idiomatic: Yuan Gongzu, Liu Yu's inspector of Qinzhou, and Shen Chengbo, Feathered Forest supervisor, were captured.

literal: Yong and Youzhi alone on horseback fled and escaped.
idiomatic: Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi fled alone on horseback and escaped.

literal: Military stores and weapons captured were beyond counting.
idiomatic: Military stores and weapons captured were beyond counting.

literal: Liu Yu sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: Liu Yu sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Day gengzi: Prince of Dongping Daofu plotted rebellion at Chang'an, killed the deputy commander, Commandant of the Majestic Steeds Wangu Zhen, Duke of Julu Li Hui, and Inspector of Yongzhou Yu Xuanming.
idiomatic: On the gengzi day Prince of Dongping Daofu plotted rebellion at Chang'an, killing the deputy commander Wangu Zhen, Commandant of the Majestic Steeds, Li Hui, Duke of Julu, and Yu Xuanming, inspector of Yongzhou.

literal: Day bingwu: an edict that Minister of Works, Duke of Pingchang He Qinu, Prince of Dongyang Yuan Pi, and others were to campaign against Daofu.
idiomatic: On the bingwu day an edict ordered He Qinu, Minister of Works and Duke of Pingchang, Yuan Pi, Prince of Dongyang, and others to campaign against Daofu.

literal: Day dingwei: Daofu's Major Duan Taiyang attacked Daofu, beheaded him, and sent the head to the capital.
idiomatic: On the dingwei day Daofu's major Duan Taiyang attacked him, beheaded him, and sent the head to the capital.

literal: Daofu's brothers were all executed.
idiomatic: Daofu's brothers were all executed.

literal: Intercalary month: Prince of Dunqiu Li Jun was made Grand Preceptor.
idiomatic: In the intercalary month Li Jun, Prince of Dunqiu, was made Grand Preceptor.

literal: Liu Yu's Inspector of Qingzhou Shen Wenxiu and Inspector of Jizhou Cui Daogu each sent envoys asking to submit their provinces inward; an edict that General Who Pacifies the East Changsun Ling and General Who Pacifies the South, Duke of Guangling Hou Qiongqi, were to go to their aid.
idiomatic: Shen Wenxiu, Liu Yu's inspector of Qingzhou, and Cui Daogu, inspector of Jizhou, each sent envoys asking to submit their provinces inward; an edict ordered Changsun Ling, General Who Pacifies the East, and Hou Qiongqi, General Who Pacifies the South and Duke of Guangling, to go to their aid.

literal: Second month: an edict that Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs, General Who Campaigns South Murong Baiyao, with fifty thousand cavalry, was to encamp at Que'ao as eastern-route reserve.
idiomatic: In the second month an edict ordered Murong Baiyao, bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of all military affairs, and General Who Campaigns South, with fifty thousand cavalry, to encamp at Que'ao as reserve for the eastern route.

literal: Prince of Jiyin Xiaoxincheng died.
idiomatic: Prince of Jiyin Xiaoxincheng died.

literal: Goryeo, Kumo Xi, Jufufu, Yuyuling, Rilian, Pili'er, Khotan, and other states each sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: Goryeo, Kumo Xi, Jufufu, Yuyuling, Rilian, Pili'er, Khotan, and other states each sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Liu Yu's Administrator of Dongping Shen Zuan garrisoned Wuyan, blocked and cut off the king's envoys; an edict that General Who Campaigns South Murong Baiyao was to command the armies to attack him.
idiomatic: Shen Zuan, Liu Yu's administrator of Dongping, garrisoned Wuyan, blocked the king's envoys, and cut off communications; an edict ordered Murong Baiyao, General Who Campaigns South, to command the armies against him.

literal: Third month, day jiayin: it was taken.
idiomatic: In the third month, on the jiayin day, it was taken.

literal: Shen Wenxiu and Cui Daogu again rebelled and returned to Liu Yu; Baiyao turned his army to campaign against them and took three of Liu Yu's garrisons—Feicheng, Yuanmiao, and Migou.
idiomatic: Shen Wenxiu and Cui Daogu again rebelled and returned to Liu Yu; Baiyao turned his army against them and took three of Liu Yu's garrisons—Feicheng, Yuanmiao, and Migou.

literal: Summer, fourth month: Baiyao attacked Shengcheng; the garrison commander Fang Chongji fled.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Baiyao attacked Shengcheng; the garrison commander Fang Chongji fled.

literal: Autumn, eighth month: Baiyao attacked Licheng.
idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn Baiyao attacked Licheng.

literal: Day dingyou: the court traveled in person to the stone cave temple on Mount Wuzhou.
idiomatic: On the dingyou day the court traveled in person to the stone cave temple on Mount Wuzhou.

literal: Day wushen: the imperial son Hong was born; a general amnesty; the era name was changed.
idiomatic: On the wushen day the imperial son Hong was born; a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.

literal: Ninth month, day renzi: Goryeo, Khotan, Pulan, and Sogdiana each sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the renzi day, Goryeo, Khotan, Pulan, and Sogdiana each sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Day dingsi: Duke of Fenyang Li Bai was advanced in rank to Prince of Liang.
idiomatic: On the dingsi day Li Bai, Duke of Fenyang, was advanced in rank to Prince of Liang.

literal: That month: an edict granted cloth to the poor of the Six Garrisons, three bolts per person.
idiomatic: That month an edict granted cloth to the poor of the Six Garrisons, three bolts per person.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day guimao: a hunt was held at Nan'anchi.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the guimao day, a hunt was held at Nan'anchi.

literal: Prince of Puyang Kongque, for the offense of negligence, was demoted in rank to duke.
idiomatic: Kongque, Prince of Puyang, for the offense of negligence, was demoted in rank to duke.

literal: Second year, spring, second month, day guiwei: a hunt was held on Western Mountain; the Emperor personally shot tigers and leopards.
idiomatic: In the second month of spring of the second year, on the guiwei day, a hunt was held on Western Mountain; the emperor personally shot tigers and leopards.

literal: Cui Daogu and Liu Yu's garrison commander of Liangzou and Administrator of Pingyuan Liu Xiubin each surrendered their cities.
idiomatic: Cui Daogu and Liu Xiubin, Liu Yu's garrison commander of Liangzou and administrator of Pingyuan, each surrendered their cities.

literal: That month bandits in Xuzhou, Sima Xiufu, styled themselves King of Jin; General Wei Yuan suppressed and pacified them.
idiomatic: That month Sima Xiufu, a bandit leader in Xuzhou, styled himself King of Jin; General Wei Yuan suppressed and pacified him.

literal: Third month: Baiyao advanced to besiege Dongyang.
idiomatic: In the third month Baiyao advanced to besiege Dongyang.

literal: Day wuwu: Liu Yu sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: On the wuwu day Liu Yu sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day xinchou: Duke of Nanjun Li Hui was made General Who Campaigns South, with Equipage Equal to the Three Directors, Commander-in-Chief of the Military Affairs of the Passes West, and Inspector of Yongzhou; he was advanced in rank to prince.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the xinchou day, Li Hui, Duke of Nanjun, was made General Who Campaigns South with equipage equal to the Three Directors, commander-in-chief of the military affairs of the passes west and inspector of Yongzhou, and advanced in rank to prince.

literal: Goryeo, Kumo Xi, Khitan, Jufufu, Yuyuling, Rilian, Pili'er, Chiliushou, Ximandan, A'dahe, Yuzhenhou, Khotan, Persia, and other states each sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: Goryeo, Kumo Xi, Khitan, Jufufu, Yuyuling, Rilian, Pili'er, Chiliushou, Ximandan, A'dahe, Yuzhenhou, Khotan, Persia, and other states each sent envoys with tribute.

literal: [2] Fifth month, day yimao: a hunt was held on Mount Guo; then the court visited Fanchi.
idiomatic: [2] In the fifth month, on the yimao day, a hunt was held on Mount Guo; then the court visited Fanchi.

literal: Day xinyou: returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the xinyou day the court returned to the palace.

literal: Sixth month, day gengchen: because Henan had opened new lands, a partial amnesty was proclaimed in the capital for offenses below capital punishment.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the gengchen day, because Henan had opened new lands, a partial amnesty was proclaimed in the capital for offenses below capital punishment.

literal: Prince of Changli Feng Xi was made Grand Tutor.
idiomatic: Feng Xi, Prince of Changli, was made Grand Tutor.

literal: Autumn, ninth month, day xinhai: the imperial uncle Zhen was enfeoffed as Prince of Nan'an, Changshou as Prince of Chengyang, Tailuo as Prince of Zhangwu, and Xiu as Prince of Anding.
idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn, on the xinhai day, the imperial uncle Zhen was enfeoffed as Prince of Nan'an, Changshou as Prince of Chengyang, Tailuo as Prince of Zhangwu, and Xiu as Prince of Anding.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day xinchou: the Emperor led a hunt at Lengquan.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the xinchou day, the emperor led a hunt at Lengquan.

literal: Eleventh month: twenty-seven provinces and garrisons suffered flood and drought; granaries were opened for relief.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month twenty-seven provinces and garrisons suffered flood and drought; granaries were opened for relief.

literal: Twelfth month, day jiawu: an edict stated: "Recently Zhang Yong, deluded and in turmoil, dared resist the king's majesty; bones lie exposed on the plains and marshes, and the maimed and ruined are not few.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the jiawu day, an edict stated, "Recently Zhang Yong, deluded and in turmoil, dared resist the king's majesty; bones lie exposed on the plains and marshes, and the maimed and ruined are not few.

literal: The living and dead suffer injustice and pain; We are deeply moved with pity.
idiomatic: The living and dead suffer injustice and pain; we are deeply moved with pity.

literal: The people of the realm are one; the commanderies and counties may be charged: soldiers of Zhang Yong's army who are maimed and ruined are to be permitted to return south of the Yangtze;
idiomatic: The people of the realm are one; let the commanderies and counties be charged: soldiers of Zhang Yong's army who are maimed and ruined are to be permitted to return south of the Yangtze;

literal: those whose bare bones lie in the wild grass are to be gathered and buried."
idiomatic: those whose bare bones lie in the wild grass are to be gathered and buried."

literal: " That month more than ten states including Ximandan each sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: That month more than ten states including Ximandan each sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day renchen: Liu Yu sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the renchen day, Liu Yu sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Day bingchen: the imperial son was given the name Hong; a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
idiomatic: On the bingchen day the imperial son was given the name Hong; a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

literal: Day dingyou: a hunt was held on Mount Guo.
idiomatic: On the dingyou day a hunt was held on Mount Guo.

literal: Fifth month: the people of Qingzhou were relocated to the capital.
idiomatic: In the fifth month the people of Qingzhou were relocated to the capital.

literal: Sixth month, day xinwei: the imperial son Hong was installed as crown prince.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the xinwei day, the imperial son Hong was installed as crown prince.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: the Rouran state sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn the Rouran state sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Winter, tenth month: Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Preceptor, Prince of Dunqiu Li Jun died.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Li Jun, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Preceptor, and Prince of Dunqiu, died.

literal: Eleventh month: the separate division chief of Tuyuhun, Baiyang Tiduhan, led his households inward in submission.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month Baiyang Tiduhan, a separate division chief of Tuyuhun, led his households inward in submission.

literal: Duke of Xiangcheng Han Tui was advanced in rank to prince.
idiomatic: Han Tui, Duke of Xiangcheng, was advanced in rank to prince.

literal: Fourth year, spring, first month: an edict that eleven provinces and garrisons had famished people; granaries were opened for relief.
idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the fourth year an edict noted that eleven provinces and garrisons had famished people; granaries were opened for relief.

literal: Second month: Prince of Dongjun Lu Dingguo was made Minister of Works.
idiomatic: In the second month Lu Dingguo, Prince of Dongjun, was made Minister of Works.

literal: Goryeo, Kumo Xi, and Khitan each sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: Goryeo, Kumo Xi, and Khitan each sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Tuyuhun's Shibin did not present tribute and service; an edict that Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Campaigns West, Prince of Shangdang Changsun Guan was to campaign against him.
idiomatic: Shibin of Tuyuhun did not present tribute and service; an edict ordered Changsun Guan, bearer of the staff of authority, General Who Campaigns West, and Prince of Shangdang, to campaign against him.
